title: Former Treasury Chief Warns AI Boom Shows 2008 Warning Signs
excerpt: Hank Paulson looked at the AI spending boom and recognized a pattern he watched up close in 2008. His warning has nothing to do with a crash, and everything...
content_html:
Quick Read

  • Paulson warns NVDA-fueled AI capex mirrors 2008's circular risk: chip vendors fund AI labs that buy their chips, concentrating risk inside the loop.

  • AI will quickly hollow out white-collar roles in legal, coding, and analysis even as headline unemployment at 4.2% masks the damage.

  • Don't wait: the analyst who called NVIDIA in 2010 just revealed his top 10 AI stocks. See the full list FREE now.

The man who ran Treasury during the last real financial crisis went on CNBC Tuesday from the Aspen Economic Strategy Group, sitting alongside Tim Geithner, and refused to pick a side. Hank Paulson steered a middle course between Bezos-style AI utopianism and Amodei-style civilizational alarm. He looked at the AI capex boom and saw a pattern from 2008, echoing its shape rather than its crash.

That shape is money moving in a circle. For a retail investor watching NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA)-fueled index gains alongside a job market where JOLTS openings just fell to 7.36 million from 7.585 million in April, the Paulson framing matters.

The Circular Money Loop Paulson Is Watching

Here is the setup in his own words. "The suppliers of chips and compute, you know, making investments in the customers. So they've got the capacity to buy and customers that need the chips, making investments in some of the suppliers to make sure they've got them." He was careful to say nothing nefarious is happening. Everyone acts rationally inside their own contract.

The problem is what happens when the same dollar shows up on three different balance sheets. A chip vendor invests in an AI lab. The AI lab uses that money to buy chips from the vendor. The vendor books revenue, its stock rises, and it recycles the gain into the next round of customer financing. When demand is real, this looks like a flywheel. When demand softens, the same wiring runs in reverse, because the supplier's revenue, the customer's spending power, and the equity valuation propping up the arrangement are the same dollar wearing three hats.

Don't wait: the analyst who called NVIDIA in 2010 just revealed his top 10 AI stocks. See the full list FREE now.

Think of climbers roped together on a cliff. Fine on the way up. When one slips, everyone learns how tightly they were tied. Paulson's point is that risk is concentrated inside the loop, which is why he says a correction is inevitable even if he is not calling a date.

The White Collar Jobs Shock

Then he turned to labor. "In terms of white collar workers, okay, there's going to be a lot of a lot of displacement and it's going to happen so quickly." That word, quickly, is the load-bearing one.

这位在上一次真正的金融危机期间执掌财政部的人周二在 CNBC 上从阿斯彭经济战略集团 (Aspen Economic Strategy Group) 与蒂姆·盖特纳 (Tim Geithner) 坐在一起，并拒绝选边站。 汉克·保尔森（Hank Paulson）在贝佐斯式的人工智能乌托邦主义和阿莫代式的文明警报之间走了一条中间路线。 他观察了人工智能资本支出的繁荣，发现了 2008 年的模式，与其形态相呼应，而不是崩溃。

那个形状就是钱在绕圈移动。 对于关注 NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) 推动的指数上涨以及就业市场 JOLTS 职位空缺从 4 月份的 758.5 万降至 736 万的散户投资者来说，保尔森的框架很重要。

保尔森正在关注的循环资金循环

这是他自己的话的设置。 “你知道，芯片和计算供应商正在对客户进行投资。 因此，他们有能力购买芯片，也有需要芯片的客户，并对一些供应商进行投资，以确保他们拥有芯片。” 他小心翼翼地说没有发生任何邪恶的事情。 每个人都在自己的契约内理性行事。

问题是当同一美元出现在三个不同的资产负债表上时会发生什么。 一家芯片供应商投资了一个人工智能实验室。 人工智能实验室用这笔钱从供应商那里购买芯片。 供应商记入收入，其股票上涨，并将收益回收到下一轮客户融资中。 当需求真实存在时，这看起来就像一个飞轮。 当需求疲软时，同样的线路会反向运行，因为供应商的收入、客户的消费能力以及支撑这种安排的股权估值都是同一美元，戴着三顶帽子。

想象一下被绳子绑在悬崖上的登山者。 一路上还好。 当一个人滑倒时，每个人都会知道他们被绑得有多紧。 保尔森的观点是，风险集中在循环内部，这就是为什么他说即使他没有确定日期，调整也是不可避免的。

白领工作冲击

然后他转向劳动。 “就白领工人而言，好吧，将会有很多人失业，而且发生得很快。” 快这个词，就是承重的词。
